s1.syndrome_frame: Palpitations with tachycardia and abnormal atrial activation
salient_findings: Positive P waves in leads II, III, aVF, and V₁
Counterclockwise propagation around the mitral annulus and left atrial appendage
key_facts: 78-year-old woman
History of two prior catheter ablations for persistent atrial fibrillation
Presented with palpitations
12-lead ECG showed tachycardia
Atrial cycle length of 280 ms
Positive P waves in leads II, III, aVF, and V₁
Electroanatomic activation map showed counterclockwise propagation
Low-voltage scar at the prior mitral isthmus line
Entrainment pacing revealed postpacing intervals within 20 ms of the tachycardia cycle length at certain locations
Postpacing interval more than 20 ms longer than the cycle length when pacing adjacent to the mitral isthmus scar
Activation within the vein of Marshall matched the tachycardia cycle length

shortlist.label: Mitral Isthmus Dependent Flutter
shortlist.why_kept: Counterclockwise propagation around the mitral annulus and left atrial appendage, interrupted by a low-voltage scar at the prior mitral isthmus line

shortlist.label: Vein of Marshall Epicardial Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Activation within the vein of Marshall matched the tachycardia cycle length

shortlist.label: Scar-Mediated Atrial Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Low-voltage scar at the prior mitral isthmus line and postpacing interval more than 20 ms longer than the cycle length when pacing adjacent to the mitral isthmus scar

shortlist.label: Macroreentrant Atrial Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Electroanatomic activation map showed counterclockwise propagation and entrainment pacing revealed postpacing intervals within 20 ms of the tachycardia cycle length at certain locations

shortlist.label: Left Atrial Flutter
shortlist.why_kept: Atrial cycle length of 280 ms and positive P waves in leads II, III, aVF, and V₁

raw.rationale: The activation within the vein of Marshall matched the tachycardia cycle length, suggesting an epicardial pathway bypassing the scar, which is consistent with Vein of Marshall Epicardial Tachycardia

rejected.label: Mitral Isthmus Dependent Flutter
rejected.why: The postpacing interval was more than 20 ms longer than the cycle length when pacing adjacent to the mitral isthmus scar, indicating that the mitral isthmus is not part of the reentrant circuit

rejected.label: Scar-Mediated Atrial Tachycardia
rejected.why: While there is a low-voltage scar at the prior mitral isthmus line, the findings suggest an epicardial pathway bypassing the scar, which is more consistent with Vein of Marshall Epicardial Tachycardia

rejected.label: Macroreentrant Atrial Tachycardia
rejected.why: The electroanatomic activation map showed counterclockwise propagation, but the activation within the vein of Marshall matched the tachycardia cycle length, suggesting a more specific diagnosis of Vein of Marshall Epicardial Tachycardia

rejected.label: Left Atrial Flutter
rejected.why: The positive P waves in leads II, III, aVF, and V₁, and the atrial cycle length of 280 ms, are not specific enough to distinguish Left Atrial Flutter from other diagnoses, and the findings in the vein of Marshall are more consistent with Vein of Marshall Epicardial Tachycardia
